patch.title: NextEra Singer Solar: 200–300 MW Source Discrepancy; $350M Published Investment
patch.description: NextEra’s Singer website advertises up to 200 MW and $350 million investment, while EIA lists a 300 MW unit planned for March 2027. These published scopes need reconciliation; the earlier $145 million figure is removed.

references.title: NextEra Energy Resources — Singer Solar
Singer Solar — Project Overview
EIA Electric Power Monthly — Table 6.5 Planned Generating Capacity Additions

patch.longFormSummary:
• NextEra’s project site describes up to 200 MW in Beauregard Parish and publishes $350 million project investment. Its overview gives about 1,970 acres.
  • EIA lists Singer Solar plant 69299, unit 4519, at 300 MW with planned March 2027 completion. This differs from the operator’s 200 MW scope.
  • Timeline: March 1, 2027 represents EIA’s month-only target. The operator overview’s as-early-as-January-2026 target is stale and does not prove operation.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: EIA planned-additions table lists Singer Solar for March 2027. March 1 is month precision, not a scheduled commissioning day; operator’s January 2026 target is older and requires reconciliation.

power.note: Current operator-advertised up-to-200 MW scope. EIA lists 300 MW; scope discrepancy unresolved.

gaps: Reconcile operator 200 MW/$350M scope against EIA 300 MW/March 2027 unit; verify actual construction/COD and parcel.

patch.title: Aligned Project Phoenix: Announced 2 GW Shippingport Campus; $10B Regional Investment
patch.description: Aligned’s September 10, 2026 groundbreaking announcement describes a 2 GW campus across three facilities in Shippingport. Its $10 billion figure is estimated regional economic investment, not a disclosed construction budget for the former 264 MW tracker scope.

references.title: Aligned Data Centers and Shippingport Community Mark Revitalization of Legacy Energy Site with Groundbreaking of 2 GW “Project Phoenix” Campus

patch.longFormSummary:
• Aligned announced groundbreaking on a 2 GW, three-facility Project Phoenix campus at Shippingport Industrial Park in September 2026.
  • The developer says dedicated onsite power will serve the campus, adjacent to the former coal station being redeveloped for natural-gas generation.
  • The announcement describes approximately $10 billion in regional economic investment, not an itemized campus construction cost. The single project-price field is cleared.
  • Timeline: no commercial-operation date is published in the announcement. January 1, 2028 remains an explicitly unverified legacy estimated placeholder.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Unverified legacy 2028 year placeholder. Opened September 10, 2026 announcement confirms groundbreaking but provides no COD. Do not treat January 1 as scheduled service.

power.note: Developer-announced 2 GW campus scope; operating load and per-phase IT allocations not published.

datacenter.cooling: Closed-loop cooling; developer states zero water for operational cooling
datacenter.powerSource: Dedicated onsite power; adjacent natural-gas energy campus redevelopment
datacenter.note: Announced 2 GW campus. $10B is regional economic investment, not a verified campus construction budget. No daily water figure published.

gaps: Obtain phased capacity and service schedule, project-only budget, exact site boundaries and tenant.

patch.description: CloudHQ lists 252 MW critical IT load and 1.7 million square feet for ORD, while its overview describes configurations up to 300 MW. ComEd’s 2022 release gives a $2.5 billion announced investment; a fixed current service date remains unverified.

references.title: ORD Campus — CloudHQ
ComEd, CloudHQ Break Ground on New Hyperscale Data Center in Mount Prospect

patch.longFormSummary:
• CloudHQ’s specification table lists 252 MW critical IT load and 1.7 million square feet; its overview separately says up to 300 MW. Final configured capacity needs confirmation.
  • ComEd’s August 2022 announcement gives $2.5 billion investment and an onsite utility substation at the former United Airlines headquarters.
  • The map center is corrected to the operator’s published 42.03501, -87.95370 coordinates; imagery is regenerated for that location.
  • Timeline: the operator gives RFS within 20 months without a fixed reference date. June 1, 2027 remains an unverified legacy estimated placeholder, not a date calculated from this check.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Legacy June 1, 2027 estimate unverified. Current operator says RFS within 20 months without an anchor; do not compute a new COD from the observation date.
patch.address: CloudHQ ORD Campus, former United Airlines headquarters, Mount Prospect, Illinois; operator-published map center

power.note: Operator specification-table critical IT capacity; overview separately describes up to 300 MW.

datacenter.note: 252 MW table vs up-to-300 MW overview. Current footprint stated as 1.7M sq ft; historical budget announced $2.5B. Acreage/building count require latest-plan reconciliation.

gaps: Resolve 252/300 MW specifications, current buildings/acreage and anchored RFS date; historical $2.5B is not a final outturn cost.

patch.title: Google Project Cannoli: 1 GW Site Plan Approved in Van Buren Township
patch.description: Michigan’s PSC conditionally approved Google/DTE service contracts on October 1, 2026. Local reporting documents October 14 final site-plan approval for a 1 GW, 282.2-acre Google campus, correcting the older 231 MW scope and unsupported $2 billion price.

references.title: Case No. U-22058, DTE Electric’s Application for Approval of Special Contracts with Google LLC
Project Cannoli data center gets the go-ahead during Oct. 14 planning meeting

patch.longFormSummary:
• MPSC conditionally approved DTE/Google service contracts October 1; its decision concerns electric service and customer protections, not local land-use approval.
  • The October 21 local report describes final site-plan approval on October 14 for a 1 GW Google facility on 282.2 acres, comprising three processing buildings, an office and two network buildings.
  • The reviewed sources do not publish a total campus budget. The earlier $2 billion amount and unsupported cooling/water estimates are removed.
  • Timeline: December 1, 2027 remains an estimated legacy target pending a verified current service schedule; no exact COD is established by these sources.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Legacy December 2027 target remains unverified by the opened MPSC brief and final-plan report; day 1 is not a promised energization day.

power.note: Reported final site-plan scope; not measured operating demand or Google-funded renewable-resource total.

datacenter.powerSource: DTE Electric; conditionally approved service contracts
datacenter.note: Six structures include three data-processing, one office and two network-service buildings. 1 GW site-plan figure per October 21 reporting; operational consumption not published.

gaps: Obtain utility contract schedule, current approved water/cooling design, total cost and exact parcel coordinates.

patch.title: Prime Phoenix Avondale: 240 MW IT Campus, Five Buildings, $3B+ Investment
patch.description: Prime announced construction of the first three buildings of its five-building, 240 MW IT Phoenix campus in May 2026. The developer release describes more than $3 billion investment; unrelated Stream Phoenix chip figures have been removed.

references.title: Prime Data Centers Breaks Ground on Three Buildings at its 240MW Campus in Phoenix, Advancing $3B Investment in Avondale
Phoenix Data Centers — Prime Data Centers

patch.longFormSummary:
• Prime’s campus covers 66.5 acres, five buildings and approximately 1.3 million square feet, totaling 240 MW critical IT capacity.
  • The first three buildings are secured by an unnamed hyperscaler; Prime does not identify that tenant. Each building is 48 MW critical IT.
  • The release describes more than $3 billion investment and closed-loop cooling designed for zero process-water use. The earlier Stream Phoenix chip/generator match is unrelated and removed.
  • Timeline: construction began in May 2026; the release does not give COD. December 31, 2026 remains an unverified legacy estimated placeholder.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Unverified legacy December 31, 2026 estimate. May 21, 2026 release confirms groundbreaking, not data-hall operation; commissioned substation phase is not campus COD.

power.note: Planned campus critical IT load; 144 MW first-three-building phase is not proof of operation.

datacenter.cooling: Closed-loop air and liquid; zero process-water use design
datacenter.note: Removed wrongly matched Stream Phoenix AI-chip and generator stats. Five-building design; first three buildings leased to unnamed hyperscaler.

gaps: Verify actual data-hall RFS/COD and commissioning status; do not infer tenant or chips from another Phoenix operator.

patch.title: TeraWulf Muskie at EastPark: Proposed 1 GW Power Agreement; First Service October 2028
patch.description: Muskie is TeraWulf’s EastPark campus near Grayson, not a verified 250 MW Catlettsburg facility. Kentucky Power’s October fact sheet describes an amended 1 GW agreement awaiting PSC approval, ramping from 100 MW in October 2028 to full service in October 2029.

references.title: Muskie Data Campus Power Fact Sheet — October 2026
TeraWulf Inc. — Form 8-K, October 5, 2026
Muskie Data Campus

patch.longFormSummary:
• Kentucky Power identifies Muskie at EastPark in Boyd and Greenup counties. The October 1 amendment increases contracted scope to 1,000 MW, subject to PSC approval; original agreement remains in force until approval.
  • Timeline: proposed service begins at 100 MW in October 2028, reaching 1,000 MW by October 2029, subject to approvals and construction. October 1 is a month-only placeholder.
  • The issuer’s filing confirms the first 500 MW phase ramps in 2028 and the second phase is accelerated from 2030 to 2029.
  • The operator describes an approximately 285-acre campus. No verified campus construction budget is published in these opened sources; the earlier $1.5B figure is cleared.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Kentucky Power October 2026 fact sheet targets first 100 MW in October 2028 and full 1,000 MW October 2029, conditional on approvals/construction. Day 1 is month precision.
patch.address: Muskie Data Campus, EastPark Industrial Park, Boyd/Greenup counties near Grayson, Kentucky; map position approximate

power.note: Proposed amended service ceiling pending PSC approval, not current load; first 100 MW targeted October 2028.

datacenter.powerSource: Kentucky Power regional grid; amended contract subject to PSC approval
datacenter.note: EastPark campus, not Catlettsburg. Acreage per operator approximately 285; other filings use different controlled-land scope. Exact parcel boundary not certified.

gaps: Verify amended agreement approval and exact parcel boundary. Approximate EastPark point from US Data Centers Tracker, consistent with operator location, replaces wrong former area; imagery regenerated.

patch.title: Vantage Trident at Windler: Aurora Proposal Under Review; Capacity and Budget Unverified
patch.description: Trident is a real Vantage proposal at E-470 and East 48th Avenue in Aurora, with local reporting documenting plan review and resident opposition. The earlier 250 MW capacity and $1.5 billion construction cost were not established by the opened records.

references.title: Aurora residents claim they were blindsided by proposed data center
Vantage: Trident at Windler Campus

patch.longFormSummary:
• September 2026 local reporting identifies Vantage’s Trident application in Aurora and says a third city review was underway. The proposal is near the northwest corner of E-470 and East 48th Avenue.
  • Published building and area figures conflict across the opened reporting and campus directory. No fixed capacity, generator count or precise building area is asserted here.
  • Baxtel lists a first-building target in 2028 with expansion through 2029. This is directory reporting, not a verified operator commitment.
  • Timeline: January 1, 2028 is a year-only estimated first-building placeholder. The prior December 2027 date and unsupported $1.5B price are removed.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Baxtel lists first building in 2028 and expansion through 2029. January 1 is a low-precision estimated directory target, not operator-confirmed COD; primary permit schedule still needed.

gaps: Aurora development-portal link returned 404/login. Obtain case DA-1707-46 current approved plan, MW, cost, generator count and operator COD. Do not turn resident claims into verified capacity.

patch.title: Clearway Mosey: Proposed 500 MW Solar and Up to 850 MW Battery Storage in Nevada
patch.description: The federal permitting dashboard describes Mosey as 500 MW solar with up to 850 MW battery storage in Pahrump Valley. These are proposed capacities under environmental review; the previous 544 MW scope and $1.25 billion budget were not substantiated.

references.title: Mosey Solar Project — Federal Permitting Dashboard
Mosey Solar Project — Plan of Development

patch.longFormSummary:
• The federal dashboard describes 500 MW solar and up to 850 MW storage on approximately 3,568 acres of BLM land in Pahrump Valley, with a connection to Trout Canyon Substation.
  • The BLM plan identifies Renew Development HoldCo LLC, care of Clearway Energy Group. Federal environmental review is not a construction or operating permit.
  • A verified project budget or exact commercial-operation date was not found in these sources. The earlier $1.25 billion estimate is cleared.
  • Timeline: June 1, 2029 remains an unverified legacy estimated placeholder; permitting milestone dates must not be substituted for COD.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Unverified legacy June 2029 estimate. Opened federal permitting/project records establish proposed scope and review, not COD.

power.note: Proposed solar capacity; separate up-to-850 MW battery scope not added to generation.

gaps: Confirm current federal approval, construction schedule, COD, cost and surveyed project coordinates.

patch.description: Dominion’s current Randolph page gives 800 MW, construction as early as January 2028 and completion phases from 2030 to 2032. A historical $800M–$1.6B estimate replaces the unsupported single $1.2B figure without claiming a current final budget.

references.title: Randolph Solar — Dominion Energy
Charlotte County approves Va.’s largest solar farm

patch.longFormSummary:
• Dominion identifies an 800 MW Charlotte County project acquired from SolUnesco.
  • Timeline: construction could begin as early as January 2028, with completion in phases from 2030 to 2032. January 1, 2030 marks the beginning of the completion window, not a fixed commissioning day.
  • August 2022 reporting gave a project estimate of $800 million–$1.6 billion. The range is historical and must not be treated as a final current cost.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Current Dominion operator page gives phased completion 2030–2032. January 1, 2030 is a year-only placeholder for initial completion; January 2028 is construction, not COD.

power.note: Planned whole-project solar capacity; phased completion 2030–2032.

gaps: Current total capital budget, phase capacities, exact commissioning days and parcel geometry remain unverified.

Projects — EDF power solutions North America

patch.title: High Noon Solar: 300 MW Solar and 165 MW Battery Storage, Expected in 2027
patch.description: MGE’s operator announcement describes High Noon in Columbia County as 300 MW solar and 165 MW battery storage, with service expected in 2027. The previously shown $650 million total and September-specific service date need current scope-specific evidence.

references.title: MGE to Add More Solar with High Noon Solar Energy Center
Solar Energy — Madison Gas and Electric

patch.longFormSummary:
• MGE will own 30 MW solar and 16.5 MW battery storage; We Energies and Wisconsin Public Service own the remaining 270 MW solar and 148.5 MW storage.
  • These ownership shares correspond to a whole-project 300 MW solar array and 165 MW storage system, not 300 MW of battery storage.
  • Timeline: MGE expects service in 2027. January 1 is a year-only estimated placeholder. The single $650 million project price is cleared pending verified full-project cost.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: MGE announcement and current solar-project page say expected service in 2027. January 1 is year-only precision; September day/month not established.

power.note: Whole-project solar capacity; separate 165 MW battery capacity is retained in text, not conflated with generation.

gaps: Obtain current all-in solar/battery budget, phase-specific COD and exact site/media alignment.

patch.title: Amazon’s Sunstone Solar: 1,200 MW Solar and Up to 7,200 MWh Storage Approval
patch.description: Oregon’s regulator identifies Amazon subsidiary Oregon Solar 1 LLC as Sunstone’s certificate holder after a June 26, 2026 ownership amendment. The approved, not-yet-constructed project has up to 1,200 MW solar and 7,200 MWh storage; construction deadline is not COD.

references.title: Sunstone Solar Project — Oregon Department of Energy

patch.longFormSummary:
• The approved design authorizes up to 1,200 MW solar generation and 7,200 MWh battery storage in Morrow County. MWh is energy capacity, not battery discharge MW.
  • The regulator records a June 26, 2026 amendment transferring ownership to Oregon Solar 1 LLC, an Amazon subsidiary, replacing the prior Pine Gate attribution.
  • The site certificate requires construction to start by November 18, 2027. That deadline is not an operating date.
  • Timeline: no verified COD or total budget is stated on this regulator page. December 1, 2027 remains an unverified legacy estimated placeholder; the unsupported $1.8 billion price is removed.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Unverified legacy December 2027 COD placeholder. ODOE gives November 18, 2027 construction-start deadline only, not COD; project remains approved but not yet constructed.

power.note: Authorized maximum solar generation; storage energy is up to 7,200 MWh, discharge MW not established here.
